Privacy Policy

Last Updated: May 2025

EyeBall ("we", "us", or "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website or use our browser-based security services (collectively, the "Services").

1. Information We Collect

We collect information that you provide directly to us, as well as information that is generated automatically when you use our Services.

  • Personal Information: We may collect names, email addresses, and professional information when you request a demo or register for our Services.
  • Usage Data: We collect technical information about how you interact with our browser security engine, including device type, browser metadata, and anonymized security events.
  • Security Logs: As part of our core security mission, we process security-related events (such as blocked phishing attempts) to improve our threat intelligence.

2. How We Use Your Information

We use the information we collect to:

  • Provide, maintain, and improve our security technology.
  • Analyze and neutralize cyber threats in real-time.
  • Communicate with you regarding service updates and security alerts.
  • Comply with legal obligations and enforce our terms of service.

3. Data Sharing and Disclosure

We do not sell your personal data. We may share information in the following circumstances:

  • Service Providers: We share data with trusted vendors who assist us in operating our business.
  • Compliance with Law: We may disclose information if required to do so by law or in response to valid requests by public authorities.
  • Business Transfers: In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that business deal.

4. Security of Your Information

EyeBall uses enterprise-grade security measures to protect your information. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

5. Data Retention

We retain your information only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.

6. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on your location, you may have rights under various data protection laws (such as GDPR or CCPA). These may include the right to access, correct, or delete your personal information.

7. International Data Transfers

Your information may be transferred to, and maintained on, computers located outside of your state, province, country, or other governmental jurisdiction where the data protection laws may differ from those in your jurisdiction.

8. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the "Last Updated" date.

9. Contact Us

If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at info@eyeballsec.com.

Privacy Policy

Last Updated: May 2025

EyeBall ("we", "us", or "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website or use our browser-based security services (collectively, the "Services").

1. Information We Collect

We collect information that you provide directly to us, as well as information that is generated automatically when you use our Services.

  • Personal Information: We may collect names, email addresses, and professional information when you request a demo or register for our Services.
  • Usage Data: We collect technical information about how you interact with our browser security engine, including device type, browser metadata, and anonymized security events.
  • Security Logs: As part of our core security mission, we process security-related events (such as blocked phishing attempts) to improve our threat intelligence.

2. How We Use Your Information

We use the information we collect to:

  • Provide, maintain, and improve our security technology.
  • Analyze and neutralize cyber threats in real-time.
  • Communicate with you regarding service updates and security alerts.
  • Comply with legal obligations and enforce our terms of service.

3. Data Sharing and Disclosure

We do not sell your personal data. We may share information in the following circumstances:

  • Service Providers: We share data with trusted vendors who assist us in operating our business.
  • Compliance with Law: We may disclose information if required to do so by law or in response to valid requests by public authorities.
  • Business Transfers: In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that business deal.

4. Security of Your Information

EyeBall uses enterprise-grade security measures to protect your information. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

5. Data Retention

We retain your information only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.

6. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on your location, you may have rights under various data protection laws (such as GDPR or CCPA). These may include the right to access, correct, or delete your personal information.

7. International Data Transfers

Your information may be transferred to, and maintained on, computers located outside of your state, province, country, or other governmental jurisdiction where the data protection laws may differ from those in your jurisdiction.

8. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the "Last Updated" date.

9. Contact Us

If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at info@eyeballsec.com.

Privacy Policy

Version 2.1 | Effective: May 2025

1. Commitment to Privacy

At EyeBall Security, we understand that our mission—protecting your organization’s data—is inextricably linked to protecting user privacy. This policy outlines our rigorous standards for data handling, built on the principle of Privacy by Design. We strive to process data locally whenever possible to ensure maximum confidentiality.

2. Information Collection & Origin

To provide high-fidelity threat detection and DLP (Data Loss Prevention) services, we collect data in the following categories:

  • 2.1 Automatically Collected Technical Data Information regarding the browser environment, including version, OS details, IP addresses (obfuscated by default), and unique installation IDs required for license validation and security patching.
  • 2.2 Security Telemetry Metadata regarding security events, such as blocked phishing attempts, malicious script executions, and policy violation logs (e.g., unauthorized file uploads or sensitive data prompts in GenAI tools).
  • 2.3 Admin-Provided Content Configuration settings, policy definitions, and administrative contact information provided by your organization's IT or Security teams.

3. Data Processing & "Local-First" Architecture

A core differentiator of the EyeBall platform is our local processing engine. Unlike legacy cloud proxies (SASE/SSE), our DLP analysis happens on the endpoint. This means:

  • Sensitive content monitored for redaction never leaves the browser memory.
  • Only metadata about the violation (e.g., "PII detected on site X") is reported to the central management console.
  • We do not record keystrokes or screen activity outside of specific security policy enforcements defined by your company.

4. Purpose of Processing

Your data is processed exclusively for:

  • Threat Prevention: Protecting users from web-borne exploits.
  • Compliance: Providing audit logs required for regulatory standards (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2).
  • Product Improvement: Using anonymized telemetry to train our threat detection models against new zero-day attacks.

5. Data Retention & Erasure

Retention periods are determined by your organization’s subscription level and internal policy. By default, security logs are retained for 90 days. Admins may request immediate erasure of specific telemetry data via the EyeBall Management Portal.

6. Third-Party Disclosures

EyeBall Security never sells, rents, or trades your data with third parties for marketing purposes. We may share anonymized threat indicators with global security researchers to strengthen the digital ecosystem, or disclose information when legally mandated by a valid court order.

1. Commitment to Privacy

At EyeBall Security, we understand that our mission—protecting your organization’s data—is inextricably linked to protecting user privacy. This policy outlines our rigorous standards for data handling, built on the principle of Privacy by Design. We strive to process data locally whenever possible to ensure maximum confidentiality.

2. Information Collection & Origin

To provide high-fidelity threat detection and DLP (Data Loss Prevention) services, we collect data in the following categories:

  • 2.1 Automatically Collected Technical Data Information regarding the browser environment, including version, OS details, IP addresses (obfuscated by default), and unique installation IDs required for license validation and security patching.

A core differentiator of the EyeBall platform is our local processing engine. Unlike legacy cloud proxies (SASE/SSE), our DLP analysis happens on the endpoint. This means:

  • Sensitive content monitored for redaction never leaves the browser memory.
  • Only metadata about the violation (e.g., "PII detected on site X") is reported to the central management console.
  • We do not record keystrokes or screen activity outside of specific security policy enforcements defined by your company.

4. Purpose of Processing

EyeBall Security never sells, rents, or trades your data with third parties for marketing purposes. We may share anonymized threat indicators with global security researchers to strengthen the digital ecosystem, or disclose information when legally mandated by a valid court order.
